findings.title: Hermes Settings radio arrows page the book and overwrite its saved position
reproduce: Open a fresh hosted /hermes-nous.html and start reading (default Deep, screen 2 / 50).
Open the Settings gear, select Light and Serif, focus the checked Light radio (Tab from the dialog heading also reaches it).
findings.expected: Native radio wraps to Dark; current slide, progress and bookHermesNous.lastSlide stay unchanged.
findings.cause: The shared dialog keydown handler intercepts only Tab and lets radio arrows bubble. Hermes dialogOpen recognizes only the old Contents/Sources dialogs, so its document listener calls go(1) and preventDefault, suppressing native radio selection.
findings.smallestCorrection: Stop propagation of dialog keydown events at the beginning of the maintained Settings keydown handler, without preventing native Arrow/Space/Escape defaults. Synchronize the shared module into current readers. An alternative is to extend Hermes dialogOpen to every open dialog and encode that in a maintained adapter that also repairs already connected pages.
findings.diagnostic: Adding only a temporary runtime keydown stopPropagation listener restored native radio changes and preserved the actual slide in RU and EN. No source edit was made and this diagnostic does not accept the reviewed head.
findings.regressionCheck: Exercise a real ArrowRight/ArrowLeft on both Settings radio groups in Hermes while recording the current node, counter and lastSlide. Current supplied keyboard QA checks the homepage, which misses this boundary.

findings.title: First Serif activation loses reading scroll while embedded fonts decode
reproduce: Use a fresh Chrome profile at 320 x 568 so neither Serif face has been decoded.
Open /essentialism.html in Sans/Essential; reach screen three-part-cycle, titled «Исследовать, отказаться, выполнить».
Scroll its actual .slide-scroll to 40 (maximum is 87), then open Settings and select Serif for the first time. Wait for document.fonts.ready and close Settings.
findings.expected: Keep the current reading position through the first font change. In this case the final loaded Serif has the same measured scroll extent, so 40 remains a valid offset.
findings.cause: apply changes data-reading-font synchronously before the data-URL Serif faces decode. The temporary system fallback shrinks the scroll range and the browser clamps scrollTop. When the real faces restore the content height, the offset is not restored. The final paragraph moves down 29px. This is distinct from unavoidable final font-metric reflow.
findings.smallestCorrection: Ensure the required embedded Serif faces are decoded before committing the reading-font attribute, or preserve and restore the active reading scroller after font decoding/layout with clamping only against final metrics. Preserve the existing slide and synchronous theme/closure behavior.
findings.diagnostic: In a fresh document, awaiting document.fonts.load for Geist Serif and Source Serif 4 before the existing Settings selection preserved scrollTop=40 and the exact paragraph viewport coordinate. A later cached-font Sans/Serif toggle also retained 40. These are runtime diagnostics, not edits or acceptance of this head.
findings.regressionCheck: Use a cold profile and a real, nonzero scroller before the very first Serif selection. Check after fonts settle, not only DOM-node identity or a font-loaded boolean.
